minimal/112-allocator-exhausted-single-r.rationale: `q = malloc(1); p = malloc((size_t)((uintptr_t)q - 7)); return (int)((uintptr_t)p & 0xff);` — ONE request larger than the cursor by 7 bytes (malloc_proxy's 8-byte argument temporary puts the cursor at a - 8, so z = last_address - sz = -1; IvMaxAlignment = 8). Pristine upstream b9aeedcb4 (memory/concrete/impl_mem.ml:1254, the truncating-division idiom `z - (if q < 0 then -m else m)` over the EUCLIDEAN quomod = ediv_rem, :9) ADDS the remainder to the negative z and SUCCEEDS at address z' = -1 + 7 = 6: an ACTIVE allocation that is NOT 8-aligned and whose object ends ABOVE the cursor (overlapping the live argument temporary) — `Defined {value: "Specified(6)", stdout: "", stderr: "", blocked: "false"}` rc 0, against C11 §7.22.3#1 (suitably aligned; disjoint from any other object). The fork (remedy 1: the out-of-memory kill BEFORE rounding) and Lean answer `Error {msg: "MerrOther "Concrete.allocator: failed (out of memory)""}` rc 1. The idiom is ORIGINAL, not a regression: at upstream adee05e5a^ (before the 2026-05-19 commit "Remove indirect use of Z through Lem's Nat_big_num") the allocator read `let (q,m) = quomod z align in let z' = sub z (if less q zero then negate m else m)` with N = Nat_big_num, whose quomod = Big_int.quomod_big_int is ALSO Euclidean (Big_int.quomod_big_int (-1) 4 = (-1, 3); (-5) 4 = (-2, 3)); the 2026-05 refactor to Z.ediv_rem preserved the behaviour exactly — present since the allocator was written; not introduced by the 2026-05 Z refactor. Class shared-model-fix (allocator-soundness slice C1, remedy 1 of draft 44; [USER 2026-09-16] "unambiguously wrong … allowed to fix ahead of upstream"); found OBSERVABLE at upstream's bound by the part-one pre-merge audit (M1). The row retires when upstream takes the fix. The owning fork-vs-Lean lane (test_exec.sh) records the file CERB_SKIP — an oracle-side `Error` is a non-comparison in its taxonomy; Lean = fork (the same Error line) is evidenced by the three-engine report and the record.
